scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “One Sample Suffices for Matroid Prophet Inequalities against an Almighty Adversary” (preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/final.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 111 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4bcbebba49132012), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a measurable online selection rule, independent of the value distributions, with the following property. Let M = (E, I) be any finite known labeled matroid, and let (Se, Ve : e ∈ E) be mutually independent nonnegative real random variables, with Se and Ve having the same arbitrary law De. Assume E[OPTM (V )] < ∞. The rule receives exactly the sample vector S before arrivals and uses a seed R independent of S, V . For every measurable permutation rule π depending on M, the laws (De), S, V , and R, the rule accepts an independent set A, irrevocably deciding at each arrival using only the available history, and E " X e∈A Ve # ≥ 2−310 E[OPTM (V )]. (1.1)
